☕️ Good Monday afternoon. Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 769 words, a 3-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

⚡️ Situational awareness: President Trump is willing to give Iran sanctions relief and release Iranian frozen funds in return for concrete steps regarding Iran's nuclear program, U.S. officials say. More from Barak Ravid.
 
 
1 big thing: SpaceX Starship goes orbital
 
Starship launches from Starbase, Texas, this morning. Photo: Ronaldo Schemidt/AFP via Getty Images

SpaceX's next-generation Starship rocket reached Earth orbit today for the first time before being brought home early, Alex Fitzpatrick reports.

  • An explosion was visible on the company's livestream just after Starship touched down in the Pacific Ocean. The cause remains unclear.

🚀 The massive, fully reusable Starship is key to SpaceX's commercial spaceflight ambitions.

  • NASA is counting on a modified version for use as a lunar lander in its Artemis program.

Starship launched from South Texas just before 9 a.m. ET on a planned test flight of about 10 hours.

  • It was set to orbit Earth about six times before splashing down in the Pacific Ocean, west of Chile. But SpaceX decided to bring it back to Earth after only about three hours.
  • As part of the mission, Starship deployed 26 of the company's new, better-performing Starlink V3 internet satellites.
Crowds watch this morning's Starship launch. Photo: Ronaldo Schemidt/AFP via Getty Images

🌎 SpaceX said in a mission summary: "Flight tests until this point have intentionally flown passively safe suborbital trajectories to maximize public safety while allowing for maximum learning."

  • "By going to orbit, the next phase of developing Starship to be fully and rapidly reusable can begin."

What's next: SpaceX plans to eventually "catch" Starship in the arms of its launch tower — a feat it's accomplished with Super Heavy, but not Starship — but didn't make the attempt this time.

2. 🤖 Florida seeks ChatGPT halt
 
Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios. Stock: Getty Images

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier has asked for a temporary injunction against OpenAI and its ChatGPT, claiming the company can't properly regulate its own technology, Axios' Josephine Walker and Avery Lotz report.

  • The legal fight could test states' ability to restrict AI companies despite the federal government declining to enact guardrails.

Uthmeier said in a video posted to X: "Stop pretending [AI is] human. Stop selling it to kids. If Sam Altman meant what he said about slowing down, he can join our ask to the court. If he will not, we ask the court to do what OpenAI will not do for itself: protect Florida families."

  • OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri tells Axios that the company is "committed to working with Florida and other states on advancing pragmatic AI policies that apply to the entire AI industry — not just one company."

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
Police guard an entrance to RAF Fairford in southern England yesterday. Photo: Justin Tallis/AFP via Getty Images
  1. 🚔 Five British men arrested on explosives and terror charges near a U.S.-operated air force base in England have been released on bail. Get the latest.
  2. 🔎 Andrew Bailey, one of the FBI's two deputy directors, announced on X that he'll leave after just over a year in the job and return to Missouri. FBI director Kash Patel thanked him for serving. Get the latest.
  3. 🚗 The Trump administration's new fuel economy standards ease requirements for automakers to control pollution from gas-powered cars and light trucks. Go deeper.
  4. A New York prosecutor has reopened an investigation into gang rape allegations at a Cornell University fraternity in response to a lawsuit filed by a woman who says she was sexually assaulted in 2024 by seven students after being plied with alcohol and drugs. Get the latest.
David Zervos talks to CNBC on the NYSE floor last year. Photo: Jeenah Moon/Reuters

🏦 Treasury coming: David Zervos, a longtime Wall Street strategist known for his out-of-consensus views, is joining the Trump administration as a senior adviser to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

  • Zervos spent over 15 years at Jefferies, most recently as the firm's chief market strategist. Zervos has been a familiar face on financial television, where his long hair made him a recognizable presence among strategists. More from Courtenay Brown.

👋 Treasury going: Luke Pettit, who was instrumental in launching Trump Accounts for children, will leave the Treasury Department for the private sector in October after the next milestone for Trump Accounts, the kickoff of auto-enrollment.

  • Pettit was Assistant Secretary for Financial Institutions and, beginning last year, Acting Under Secretary for Domestic Finance. He also worked on fast-evolving AI policy as leader of the Office of Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection.
 
 
4. 🐊 1 sports thing: Gators crack top 10
 
Data: AP; Table: Axios Visuals

The University of Florida made a massive jump in the latest college football AP Top 25 rankings, landing in the top 10 for the first time in five years.

🏈 The Gators' 24-point win over then-No. 4 Mississippi under first-year coach Jon Sumrall earned them a 13-spot promotion to No. 8.

  • That's their highest ranking since 2020, and first top-10 appearance since 2021.

🥇 Texas, Georgia and Notre Dame still hold the top three spots.
